rows.title: Yet another recession indicator is flashing as consumer confidence declines sharply in September
rows.standfirst: Consumer confidence has dropped below key thresholds, challenging Fed policymakers and Wall Street’s bullish market view.

rows.title: Shark Tank’s Kevin O’Leary blasts Gen Z who love to job-hop every six months: ‘That’s a red flag’
rows.standfirst: Gen Z’s job-hopping obsession might be career suicide, warns the ‘Shark Tank’ multimillionaire investor: He’d throw their resume straight ‘into the garbage.’

rows.title: Stocks shrug off government shutdown but bond yields sink on ADP payrolls report showing weak job growth and a huge August revision
rows.standfirst: Employers outside the government actually cut 32,000 more jobs than they added, according to ADP, while August was revised down to a loss of 3,000 jobs.

rows.title: The economy is just getting stronger, not weaker, and ‘we in the economics profession need to look ourselves in the mirror,’ top analyst says
rows.standfirst: “The consensus has been wrong since January,” Apollo Global Management chief economist Torsten Sløk wrote on Wednesday.

rows.title: More bad news for Gen Z grads: Even LinkedIn’s CEO is saying the future of work won’t belong to people with degrees anymore
rows.standfirst: LinkedIn CEO Ryan Roslansky said Ivy League diplomas won’t get Gen Z hopefuls far in the job hunt. Warren Buffett and Mark Zuckerberg agree college isn’t needed for success.

rows.title: Netflix will pay you up to $700K per year—and let you work fully remote—if you can harness AI to make employees more productive
rows.standfirst: This will be a competitive position, to say the least.

rows.title: The Gen Z hiring nightmare is real, but AI is a ‘lightning strike’ not a ‘house fire,’ Yale economist says
rows.standfirst: Stanford made waves with a paper saying AI is having a “significant” impact on entry-level jobs. Not so fast, Yale’s Martha Gimbel told Fortune.

rows.title: The AI jobs apocalypse is not yet upon us, according to new data
rows.standfirst: Despite the hype and handwringing, new research from Yale has found no evidence of an AI-driven jobs apocalypse.

rows.title: UK chancellor pledges ‘youth guarantee’ for Gen Zers 18 months out of work: a job, a trade, or college placement
rows.standfirst: The Labour Party looks to wrangle in high youth unemployment after a historic low in 2022.

rows.title: Economy flies blind without jobs data, unemployment claims during government shutdown
rows.standfirst: Earlier this month, Jerome Powell stressed how crucial each month is: “We’re in a meeting-by-meeting situation, and we’re going to be looking at the data.”

rows.title: Ford CEO reveals that he made sure his Gen Z son ‘had a summer job where he learned how to weld, to fabricate, to really work with his hands’
rows.standfirst: Jim Farley said his grandfather, a Ford factory worker, didn’t go to college, and if his son goes on to work in the trades, he’d be “so thrilled as a parent.”

rows.title: Millennials and Gen Zers are clamoring to break into the housing market. But this real estate expert says ‘not everyone should be an owner’
rows.standfirst: Just thinking it’s time to buy a house is not “a good reason to own a home,” the Real Deal publisher told Fortune.

rows.title: Insomnia Cookies CEO made millions selling his company to Krispy Kreme, but has a warning for entrepreneurs: ‘It can be lonely; it’s a solitary life’
rows.standfirst: Seth Berkowitz wants aspiring young people in business to know the life of an entrepreneur is “not for everyone”—especially when burnout and the pressure of raising capital set in.

rows.title: America’s landlords settle claim they used rent-setting algorithms to gouge consumers nationwide for $141 million
rows.standfirst: Greystar, the nation’s largest landlord, would pay $50 million under the proposed settlement agreement, with 25 others also settling.

rows.title: Ford CEO Jim Farley hopes AI will help blue-collar workers, but ‘it’s hard to say that today’
rows.standfirst: Tech innovations like automation have taken work away from the industry in the past, he said.

rows.title: The U.S. may mint a coin with Trump’s face despite a law he signed that prohibits collectibles with similar likenesses
rows.standfirst: A draft design harkens back to an assassination attempt during his 2024 presidential campaign and reads “FIGHT, FIGHT, FIGHT”

rows.title: The job market is weak and getting weaker, top economist says, while Trump looks to the future
rows.standfirst: “Our big year won’t be really next year—it’ll be the year after,” Trump told reporters recently.

rows.title: America saw ‘essentially no job growth’ last month, warns Moody’s, and any roles added were in three wealthy states
rows.standfirst: Moody’s warns U.S. job growth has stalled as the shutdown halts official labor data, forcing Wall Street and the Fed to rely on patchy private reports.

rows.title: How ‘The Summer I Turned Pretty’ writer went from library and Olive Garden shifts to building an empire with Netflix and Amazon deals
rows.standfirst: Jenny Han, the author behind hit series like “To All the Boys I’ve Loved Before,” said she wouldn’t change a thing about her come-up, and that working as a librarian helped her tap into what young readers were looking for.

rows.title: Trump says the American Dream is on hold because ‘big homebuilders’ are ‘sitting on’ 2 million empty lots
rows.standfirst: It’s an unusual attack, since it resembles Ezra Klein’s “abundance” thesis, and one of Trump’s top deputies is a homebuilding heir.

rows.title: Trump, Lula talk for 30 minutes, exchange numbers and Brazilian boss asks again for lifting of 40% tariff
rows.standfirst: Later, Trump posted on Truth Social that he had had a good conversation with Lula. “We discussed many things, but it was mostly focused on the Economy.”

rows.title: Former Cisco CEO John Chambers navigated the dot-com crash—now he sees the same red flags with AI
rows.standfirst: “The problem this time is that if I am right about AI moving at five times the speed of the internet, we are going to destroy jobs faster than we can replace them,” he said.

rows.title: 100 million jobs could be wiped out from the U.S. alone thanks to AI, warns Senator Bernie Sanders
rows.standfirst: It’s not just software developers who are at risk. According to the new Senate Democrat report, even nursing and fast-food jobs are set to get slashed by AI.

rows.title: Nearly 70% of Americans think the economy is on the ‘wrong track’ and even more think it’s a bad time to buy a home, Fannie Mae survey shows
rows.standfirst: Americans are short on hope about the housing market.

rows.title: America’s air traffic controller shortage is even worse during the government shutdown—but job candidates can make $145,000 per year
rows.standfirst: Air traffic controllers, expected to work without pay during the government shutdown, aren’t showing up to airports. It’s making the industry’s headcount problem even worse, with staffing down 50% in some areas.

rows.title: Why boomers keep winning in the housing market as ‘investors and second-home buyers’ continue to dominate
rows.standfirst: All-cash deals were 27.5% of the market in 2019. It’s a different world now, according to Realtor.com’s Hannah Jones and ResiClub’s Lance Lambert

rows.title: Top Wall Street economist sees 2 ways tariffs could play out—and neither is good for the average worker
rows.standfirst: Nathan Sheets, Citi’s global chief economist, told Fortune that it’s a similar situation to the “devastating” 1930s, but maybe not in the way you think.

rows.title: ‘Big Short’ investor Steve Eisman warns the U.S. economy is a ‘tale of two cities’ that ‘is not even growing 50 basis points outside of AI’
rows.standfirst: Eisman said if you erase AI infrastructure spending from projected U.S. GDP growth for 2025, the economic picture exposes a struggling consumer.

rows.title: Jamie Dimon isn’t so sure the U.S. will avoid a recession next year—even if Wall Street is convinced otherwise
rows.standfirst: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon says a U.S. recession could hit in 2026, a warning to markets not to get complacent despite strong GDP growth and AI optimism.

rows.title: Investors can’t hold back their AI bubble jitters anymore as gold pushes beyond $4,000 per ounce
rows.standfirst: Wall Street posted its first loss in seven days on Tuesday.

rows.title: The real-estate ‘winner’s curse’: Study of nearly 14 million home sales over 20 years shows you don’t want to win that bidding war
rows.standfirst: Economists at the Rochester Institute of Technology looked at a dataset covering 30 U.S. states, looking for patterns in resales and mortgage defaults.

rows.title: Billionaire investor Marc Andreessen says AI destroying jobs and making everyone poor is a ‘fallacy’—and even if that did happen, prices would drop
rows.standfirst: An AI-driven productivity boom could create an era of abundance—where $100 items might soon sell for just a penny, said Andreessen Horowitz cofounder Marc Andreessen.

rows.title: Jamie Dimon warns leaders not to ‘put their head in the sand’ about AI. ‘It is going to affect jobs’
rows.standfirst: Managers and leaders have to “get their mind working on how they’re gonna use this thing,” the JPMorgan Chase CEO said. “It’s kind of the tip of the iceberg.”

rows.title: Gen Z’s housing bust laid bare: 15 million more adults under 35 are living with their parents than a decade ago
rows.standfirst: That’s a 6.3% jump, more than double the rate of growth for the young adult population overall.

rows.title: Stripe exec says she’s hiring new grads more than ever but she’s ‘sweating’ about the Gen Z talent pipeline—and warns the era of skills is at risk
rows.standfirst: Stripe’s head of data and AI is worried that Gen Z graduates won’t get jobs as the tech continues to take over skills—and warned of having no talent pipeline in 10 years.

rows.title: Delta’s bet on wealthy Americans driving the economy is working: Premium seats are set to overtake main cabin for the first time in history
rows.standfirst: Premium is on track to overtake main cabin in 2026, a year ahead of schedule, per the third-quarter earnings call from America’s most profitable airline.

rows.title: America’s real estate is aging in place, just like its population. Investors and CEOs can’t ignore it
rows.standfirst: The wave of retirements is turning into a trickle in the real estate sector, too.

rows.title: Multimillionaire Shonda Rhimes built a billion-dollar TV empire but still hunts for discounts and clips coupons like Warren Buffett
rows.standfirst: Multimillionaire ‘Bridgerton’ producer Shonda Rhimes still hunts for bargains because ‘absolutely nothing’ changes when your dreams come true.

rows.title: AI enabled Klarna to halve its workforce—now, the CEO is warning workers that other ‘tech bros’ are sugarcoating just how badly it’s about to impact jobs
rows.standfirst: Sebastian Siemiatkowski, who told Sam Altman he wanted Klarna to be ChatGPT’s “favorite guinea pig,” says too many CEOs are downplaying how disruptive AI will really be.

rows.title: Before ‘Abbott Elementary,’ Janelle James did it all—waitressing, personal chef, party planner, sewing teacher. Now she’s making over $4 million a season
rows.standfirst: Before landing a $200,000-per-episode salary on Abbott Elementary, Janelle James did ‘every hustle in the book’ to stay afloat.

rows.title: Fed’s Chris Waller says he had a ‘great interview’ to succeed Jerome Powell and the labor market is ‘weak’ and ‘not doing great’
rows.standfirst: “There was nothing political about it,” the Fed governor told CNBC. “Just serious economic discussion.”

rows.title: New China tariffs announced during government shutdown and AI valuation debate are a ‘perfect storm coming together,’ top economist says
rows.standfirst: Expect the new round of tariffs to spur inflation and put “downward pressure” on GDP, he added.

rows.title: At this rate, the price of gold could soar to $10,000 per ounce in just three years
rows.standfirst: “If it continues on its current path, it could reach $10,000 before the end of the decade.”

rows.title: Trump’s tariff-revenue checks could create a ‘weird feedback loop’ that encourages more price hikes, analyst says
rows.standfirst: But the inflationary effects may not be as severe as Biden’s COVID-era stimulus checks were.

rows.title: Trump keeps saying he’s ‘defeated’ inflation but coffee is 21% more expensive and groceries just had their largest non-pandemic jump in a decade
rows.standfirst: Grocery prices moved up 2.7% in August from a year ago, the largest gain since 2015 outside the pandemic. Brazilian coffee beans are tariffed at 50%.

rows.title: Trump bet China would face ‘tremendous difficulties’ without U.S. consumers—Beijing just focused on the rest of the world instead
rows.standfirst: China’s trade diversification has been so successful that its export market is growing significantly despite the trade war.

rows.title: Holiday hiring forecast to fall to 16-year low as tariffs force retail pullback
rows.standfirst: Deloitte Services forecasts holiday retail sales to be up between 2.9% to 3.4% from Nov. 1 through Jan. 31, a slowdown from 2024.

rows.title: Would-be homebuyers are getting cold feet and backing out of deals at a record pace as some sellers have a ‘hard time adjusting’ to new reality
rows.standfirst: About 56,000 U.S. purchase agreements were canceled in August, representing 15.1% of homes that went under contract that month, Redfin said.

rows.title: GoFundMe CEO says the economy is so bad that more of his customers are crowdfunding just to pay for their groceries
rows.standfirst: GoFundMe’s CEO says more Americans are crowdfunding everyday essentials like groceries as high costs and strained household finances persist.

rows.title: Goldman economists on the Gen Z hiring nightmare: ‘Jobless growth’ is probably the new normal
rows.standfirst: “History also suggests that the full consequences of AI for the labor market might not become apparent until a recession hits.”

rows.title: Even workers earning more than $500,000 annually are living paycheck to paycheck—thanks to ‘lifestyle inflation,’ they’re continuing to splurge money they don’t have
rows.standfirst: America’s top earners feel just as broke as workers scraping by on less than $50,000, thanks to soaring food, housing, and luxury item costs.

rows.title: Powell just gave his strongest hint yet that rate cuts are coming, and investors are jubilant: ‘Stage is set for parabolic Q4’
rows.standfirst: Powell gave two strong signals that liquidity will soon be injected into the market.

rows.title: Powell says exactly what Wall Street wants to hear as Trump provokes soybean battle with China
rows.standfirst: Investors heard enough of what they wanted to remain bullish on further cuts.

rows.title: Gen Z’s misery is real: Most workers in this economy lack a voice and are stuck in low-quality jobs, a massive Gates-backed study finds
rows.standfirst: “We’ve seen, really, a rising tide of unhappiness, loneliness, isolation, anxiety, stress, and worry,” Stephanie Marken of Gallup told Fortune.

rows.title: Nestlé is laying off over 16,000 employees under its new CEO—and says a key motivator is ‘automation’
rows.standfirst: “This initiative is focused on transforming our ways of working,” a company spokesperson told Fortune.

rows.title: Gen Z is snubbing college as a dismal job market and sky-high tuition forces them to weigh ROI: ‘No schools are immune’
rows.standfirst: More students are heading to technical schools or the trades and passing on four-year universities.

rows.title: Yes, you can still ask for a raise in an ugly job market—experts reveal when (and how) to do it
rows.standfirst: Experts suggest asking how much your colleagues are making, for starters.

rows.title: Meta is hiring entry-level roles that pay up to $290,000 a year and require little prior experience
rows.standfirst: The $1.8 trillion tech giant is looking for software engineers, only requiring a bachelor’s degree and minimal working experience. They’re welcome job postings as many tech companies cut back on hiring entry level Gen Z staffers.

rows.title: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon says if you check your email in meetings, he’ll tell you to close it: ’it’s disrespectful’
rows.standfirst: Wall Street titan Jamie Dimon says workplace etiquette has gone off the rails—and he’s calling for a return to old-school focus in an age of AI and constant notifications.

rows.title: Goldman Sachs says the demand for gold is not just hype, and predicts the U.S. could still see a repeat of a Nixon-era spike
rows.standfirst: From 1970 to 1980, the price of gold skyrocketed more than 2,300% because of the end of the gold standard, soaring inflation, and the oil crisis.

rows.title: John Summit went from working 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. in a $65,000 job to a multimillionaire DJ—‘I make more in one show than I would in my entire accounting career’
rows.standfirst: Swapping cubicles for full-time party life, Summit is now a multi-millionaire DJ, producer and owner of his own label “Experts Only.”

rows.title: Even the author of ‘Trumponomics’ admits ‘tariffs are taxes—and taxes are bad’
rows.standfirst: Trump’s former economic advisor Stephen Moore tells Fortune tariffs have dragged down growth and raised prices, and says he’s concerned about Trump publicly dictating prices on drugs and beef.

rows.title: AI startups are leasing luxury apartments in San Francisco for staff and offering large rent stipends to attract talent
rows.standfirst: The average rent increase in San Francisco leads all other cities in the past year, according to real estate data.

rows.title: Like Jeff Bezos and Howard Schultz, Chess.com’s cofounder says people doubted his vision—with a 225 million-user empire, he’s now having the last laugh
rows.standfirst: Cofounder of Chess.com says he was “laughed out of VC rooms who said that chess would never be anything.”

rows.title: Nearly half of U.S. adults aren’t confident they could find a good job, while electricity and grocery costs are major sources of stress, poll says
rows.standfirst: The poll found that 36% of U.S. adults approve of how Trump is handling the economy, a figure that has held steady this year.

rows.title: Dow futures rally as Trump softens tone on trade war again while first tech earnings and inflation report loom
rows.standfirst: On Tuesday, Netflix and Texas Instruments are due. On Wednesday, Tesla and IBM will report, while Intel is scheduled for Thursday.

rows.title: This Gen Zer dropped out of college and is making over $100,000 repairing plane engines after 21 months of training
rows.standfirst: “I was studying mechanical engineering and I didn’t like the fact that half of my classes didn’t relate to the actual career that I wanted to get into.”

rows.title: ‘We would buy some beef from Argentina’: Trump’s plan to counter the flesh-eating parasite keeping red meat prices skyhigh
rows.standfirst: U.S. beef prices have been stubbornly high for a variety of reasons.

rows.title: As workers fear for AI job cuts, Open AI co-founder says AI agents will take a decade before they even work: ‘They don’t have enough intelligence’
rows.standfirst: For employees worried that AI agents could take their jobs, Andrej Karpathy, co-founder of OpenAI says the technology is still far from perfect.

rows.title: J. Crew CEO bought her first interview suit at the iconic retailer. Now she wants to capitalize on nostalgia

rows.title: Florida’s housing market was skewed wildly by the pandemic. It’s finally coming to grips with a ‘realistic middle ground’
rows.standfirst: Now might not be the right time to sell your house in Florida.

rows.title: Trump immigration policies would slash workforce estimate by 15.7 million and slow GDP growth by a third over the next decade, study says
rows.standfirst: “Immigrants both create demand for the goods and services produced by U.S.-born workers and work alongside them in ways that increase productivity for both groups.”

rows.title: ‘If there’s no bottom rung on the ladder, it’s really hard to leap up’: Nonprofits focused on Gen Z employment get $25m Citi Foundation windfall
rows.standfirst: Citi Foundation identified youth employability as the theme for its $25 million Global Innovation Challenge this year.

rows.title: Sam Altman’s OpenAI is coming for Wall Street’s grunt workers as AI continues to transform the entry level
rows.standfirst: Experts say automation of low-level tasks in finance will “transform” rather than “eliminate” roles on Wall Street.

rows.title: Egypt’s crisis becomes Europe’s business problem as inflation soars and Suez revenues collapse
rows.standfirst: Last year, Brussels announced a package worth about $8.6 billion for cash-strapped Egypt.

rows.title: Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky challenges founders with a critical question if they aspire to emulate his success
rows.standfirst: Brian Chesky says that before chasing the dream of building the next Airbnb, aspiring entrepreneurs must answer one critical question—and the best answer he’s ever heard is: “Because if I don’t do it, no one else will.”

rows.title: The ‘quiet alarm bell’ on U.S. health costs: Employers are backed into a corner, and workers are paying the price
rows.standfirst: Family premiums neared about $27,000 in 2025 and could climb further next year, intensifying pressure on employers to raise deductibles, tighten GLP‑1 coverage, and redesign plans.

rows.title: JPMorgan’s new $3 billion skyscraper is open 24/7—and bankers can order coffee straight to their desks
rows.standfirst: There’s also a vegan restaurant and a cafe that serves protein shakes from an Airstream trailer.

rows.title: Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon says AI won’t destroy human jobs—’Yes, job functions will change…but I’m excited about it’
rows.standfirst: Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon said every CEO he speaks with is focused on AI automation, and despite “volatility” around jobs, humans will adjust to a new normal.

rows.title: The U.S. housing market is in spooky season: 15% of home sellers are getting ghosted by buyers
rows.standfirst: “It’s a buyer’s market in most of the U.S.,” according to Redfin.

rows.title: Top economist on the economy’s dirty truth: The only people who feel good are ‘making over $200,000’ and ‘have large stock portfolios’

rows.title: Inflation is still ‘the dog that didn’t bark’ as delayed CPI report shows cooler-than-expected rise to 3%
rows.standfirst: Chris Zaccarelli of Northlight Asset Management told Fortune that inflation reminds him of “a Sherlock Holmes’ story.”

rows.title: ‘Now it’s like, ‘OK, you’re in office. I’m still getting done dirty at the grocery store”: Hispanic voters’ inflation fatigue weighs on Trump polling
rows.standfirst: The October survey from AP-NORC finds that 25% of Hispanic adults have a “somewhat” or “very” favorable view of Trump.

rows.title: Parents offering $240K to tutor their one-year-old—the job ad calls for someone ‘from a socially appropriate background’ to prepare their toddler for top schools
rows.standfirst: The CEO of Tutors International says the salary is not shocking for wealthy families.

rows.title: These 2 states will determine if the U.S. slips into a recession while one more enters the danger zone, top economist says
rows.standfirst: “This state-level picture mirrors the national trend: The U.S. economy is not in recession, but it is struggling to avoid one.”

rows.title: Social Security payments to go up 2.8% next year while polls show three-fourths of seniors think 3% isn’t enough to keep up with rising prices
rows.standfirst: Recipients received a 2.5% cost-of-living boost in 2025 and a 3.2% increase in their benefits in 2024, after a historically large 8.7% benefit increase in 2023.

rows.title: Founder of $100 million company says she quit her day job to rebuild her father’s Cape Cod chip empire—and there ‘wasn’t time’ to worry about nepotism
rows.standfirst: Serial entrepreneur Nicole Bernard Dawes scaled her own multimillion-dollar brands, Late July and Nixie, after getting Cape Cod chips back on track: “I’m not my father. That was his dream and his company.”

rows.title: Stop blaming Gen Z: the workforce system is broken. Here’s how leaders can step up
rows.standfirst: It’s a terrible idea to write off a whole generation as unfit for duty.

rows.title: The housing market’s fall surprise: Buyers are back, and Zillow says the momentum isn’t over yet
rows.standfirst: With buyers gaining ground in more cities and rates sliding further in October, Zillow says the fall season could extend the market’s momentum.

rows.title: Why is Washington acting like the U.S. is in a recession?
rows.standfirst: On paper, the economy is growing and unemployment is low. But federal government policymakers are behaving like there is an imminent crisis.

rows.title: Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway and Zillow say mortgage rates can’t fall enough for Americans to afford a home
rows.standfirst: Mortgage rates are more than 6%, but one Zillow analyst says even a 0% interest rate still wouldn’t make a typical home affordable in some areas.

rows.title: Candy inflation has spooked so many consumers almost 80% say they’re forced to scale back how much to buy for Halloween
rows.standfirst: Of the 6,000+ shoppers surveyed, 83% said they’re capping their candy spending at $100.

rows.title: The world is about $4.5 trillion short of securing a sustainable food supply for the future, global food and ag business CEO says
rows.standfirst: Verghese estimated the world requires 593 million hectares of land—twice the size of India—every year for crop cultivation at current productivity growth rates.

rows.title: The Gen Z job crisis is real: 1.2 million recent grads in the U.K. competed for just 17,000 open roles
rows.standfirst: Rob Breare, CEO of independent U.K. school system Malvern College International, said at Fortune’s Global Forum that AI is upending the job hunt as we know it, forcing Gen Z to ask their colleges for help.

rows.title: How employee ownership can uplift Gen Z’s labor force
rows.standfirst: The newest generation of American workers feels unheard in the places that depend most on their ideas and energy.

rows.title: Wealthy family in New Jersey posts tutoring job for $264,000 a year—complete with 45 days vacation and a guesthouse
rows.standfirst: The private tutor must have expertise in the U.S. curriculum, an “easygoing” personality, and a “good sense of humor.”

rows.title: Trump tells Japan’s first woman Prime Minister she has a ‘very strong handshake’ in Tokyo meeting
rows.standfirst: A putter from Shinzo Abe, gold golf balls, and American steak — Takaichi played to Trump’s taste for “golden age” diplomacy in Tokyo.

rows.title: As Gen Z faces the white collar freeze in hiring, law and business school applications are soaring
rows.standfirst: Gen Z is rushing back to the classroom to dodge AI disruption as law-school applications have jumped 33% compared to this time last year.

rows.title: From retail to tech, here are the 10 corporations that recently announced mass layoffs
rows.standfirst: Companies are pointing to factors like tariff costs, shifts in consumer spending, and investments in AI that have led them to let go of thousands.

rows.title: Real estate CEO says the luxury industry is all about one thing: a ‘return on ego’
rows.standfirst: DarGlobal CEO Ziad El Chaar sees co-branded real estate—what he calls the “limited edition of real estate”—as both a cultural anchor and a magnet for the world’s elite.

rows.title: Everyone thinks AI is replacing factory workers, but Amazon’s layoffs show it’s coming for middle management first
rows.standfirst: As Amazon slashes 14,000 white-collar roles and the U.S. approaches a million job cuts this year, AI’s first major labor casualty might be emerging.

rows.title: You can expect a 0.25% cut from the Fed, says Wall Street, but little economic insight from Powell—after all, he doesn’t have much to go on
rows.standfirst: “Chair Powell’s press conference will pivot away from economic data—given its scarcity—and instead focus on balance sheet policy, the policy framework review, and financial stability,” Deutsche Bank says.

rows.title: Gen Z is leading a blue-collar revolution as more Americans lose faith in college education
rows.standfirst: U.S. colleges are being questioned by the Trump administration, while citizens wonder if costly degrees are even worth it anymore, pushing Gen Z into blue-collar roles.

rows.title: These are the U.S. cities where Americans can actually afford to live on a single person’s income—and the ones out-of-budget for singletons
rows.standfirst: To measure affordability, analysts used the rule that rent shouldn’t exceed 30% of income. In New York, that means nearly $4,000 a month for a studio apartment.

rows.title: Powell cuts rates in the dark in historic move, with no jobs data and Trump heckling from abroad
rows.standfirst: For the first time in modern history, the Fed cut rates without jobs data, acting amid a government shutdown, rising unemployment, and open pressure from the president, who wants Powell gone.

rows.title: America’s officially running out of pennies — and it’s costing retailers millions
rows.standfirst: “Let’s rip the waste out of our great nation’s budget, even if it’s a penny at a time,” President Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social.

rows.title: Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky says employers need to hire Gen Z even if ‘AI can do the interns’ work’—or one day, the bots will outnumber bosses
rows.standfirst: Airbnb cofounder and CEO Brian Chesky warns AI isn’t “magic,” and companies that skip out on hiring Gen Z risk losing future CEOs to automation.

rows.title: Jerome Powell says the AI hiring apocalypse is real: ‘Job creation is pretty close to zero’
rows.standfirst: Powell said the Fed is walking a tightrope as AI-fueled investment props up growth but erodes hiring.

rows.title: Goldman Sachs survey says only 11% of companies are actively linking layoffs to AI—but the real shock is yet to come
rows.standfirst: Just under half of companies are for now using AI to boost productivity and revenue.

rows.title: Since ChatGPT launched, job openings are down 30% while the stock market is up 70%. One economist says the true culprit isn’t AI, but monetary policy
rows.standfirst: The relationship between job openings and stock market performance has been called “the scariest chart in the world.”

rows.title: The government shutdown won’t be completely recouped—and it could cost the economy up to $14 billion, estimates say
rows.standfirst: The report says lost goods and services from furloughed workers’ downtime won’t be regained once the government reopens.

rows.title: Not even blue-collar jobs are safe from automation—the era of robots is here and for $20K you can already buy your first robo housekeeper

frame: Union of four fixed economic tags
